validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n    \n    // 1. }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CedETsLBga7nuY1eXGjCe","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017KmwqHw7uEinKSGugtEbCH","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/evals/20260901-162328/floydwarshall_claude-opus-5-cc-medium_omp_r1/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <sys/mman.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr unsigned int INF = 1000000000;\nconstexpr unsigned int MAX_DISTANCE = 200;\n\n// Index calculation for flattened 2D array\ninline constexpr size_t idx2(const size_t i, const size_t j, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    return j * n + i;\n}\n\n// The matrices are stored row-major with respect to the (i, j) access pattern used by the\n// algorithm below: element (i, j) lives at i * numNodes + j == idx2(j, i, numNodes).\n\n// Spread the pages of a matrix over the NUMA nodes of the machine via parallel first touch.\n// The vector's own value-initialization already faulted every page onto the node of the\n// initializing thread, so the mapping is dropped first (private anonymous memory reads back\n// as zero afterwards, which is exactly the state the vector was in).\nstatic void firstTouchDistribute(std::vector<unsigned int>& v) {\n    const size_t bytes = v.size() * sizeof(unsigned int);\n    const long pageSize = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);\n    if (pageSize > 0 && bytes > static_cast<size_t>(pageSize)) {\n        const uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(v.data());\n        const uintptr_t pageMask = static_cast<uintptr_t>(pageSize) - 1;\n        const uintptr_t start = (base + pageMask) & ~pageMask;\n        const uintptr_t end = (base + bytes) & ~pageMask;\n        if (end > start) {\n            madvise(reinterpret_cast<void*>(start), end - start, MADV_DONTNEED);\n        }\n    }\n\n    unsigned int* const data = v.data();\n    const size_t count = v.size();\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {\n        data[i] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializeDistanceMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes,\n                              const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - Requires C/P to be distinct from\n// A and B, which lets the k loop be sunk innermost so the destination row stays in registers.\nstatic inline void tileRelaxDisjoint(unsigned int* __restrict c, unsigned int* __restrict p,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict a,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict b, const size_t n,\n                                     const size_t kBase, const size_t ni, const size_t nj,\n                                     const size_t nk) {\n    for (size_t ii = 0; ii < ni; ++ii) {\n        unsigned int* const cRow = c + ii * n;\n        unsigned int* const pRow = p + ii * n;\n        const unsigned int* const aRow = a + ii * n;\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n            const unsigned int aik = aRow[kk];\n            const unsigned int* const bRow = b + kk * n;\n            const unsigned int kValue = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kk);\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n                const unsigned int candidate = aik + bRow[jj];\n                const unsigned int current = cRow[jj];\n                const bool better = candidate < current;\n                cRow[jj] = better ? candidate : current;\n                pRow[jj] = better ? kValue : pRow[jj];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Same relaxation, but for tiles where C overlaps A and/or B (the pivot tile and the tiles of\n// the pivot row/column). <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr unsigned int INF = 1000000000;\nconstexpr unsigned int MAX_DISTANCE = 200;\n\n// Index calculation for flattened 2D array\ninline constexpr size_t idx2(const size_t i, const size_t j, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    return j * n + i;\n}\n\nvoid initializeDistanceMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes, \n                              const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes * numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[i] = rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n    }\n    \n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializePathMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            path[idx2(i, j, numNodes)] = j;\n            path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = i;\n        }\n        path[idx2(j, j, numNodes)] = j;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm\n    // For each intermediate node k\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // For each source node i\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            // For each destination node j\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n                \n                if (newDist < distIJ) {\n                    dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n                    path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = k;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n    \n    // 1. Diagonal should be zero\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        if (dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] != 0) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: diagonal element [%zu,%zu] is not zero\\n\", i, i);\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // 2. Triangle inequality: dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] >= dist[i][j]\n    // Check a sample of paths to avoid O(n^3) validation time\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++j) {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                // Check for overflow before addition\n                if (distIK < INF && distKJ < INF) {\n                    if (distIK + distKJ < distIJ) {\n                        printf(\"Validation failed: triangle inequality violated at [%zu,%zu,%zu]\\n\", \n                               i, j, k);\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of nodes in the graph (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numNodes = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numNodes = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of nodes: %zu\\n\", numNodes);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrices\n    std::vector<unsigned int> dist(numNodes * numNodes);\n    std::vector<unsigned int> path(numNodes * numNodes);\n    \n    // Initialize\n    printf(\"Initializing graph...\\n\");\n    initializeDistanceMatrix(dist, numNodes, 1, MAX_DISTANCE);\n    initializePathMatrix(path, numNodes);\n    \n    // Run Floyd-Warshall\n    printf(\"Computing shortest paths...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    floydWarshall(dist, path, numNodes);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate operations per second\n    // Floyd-Warshall has O(n³) complexity\n    double ops = (double)numNodes * numNodes * numNodes;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation (integer hash-based)\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results_int(dist, \"DistanceMatrix\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResult(dist, numNodes);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n","userModified":false}}

The b tile is packed into a contiguous scratch buffer\n// first: reading it at the full matrix stride causes cache-set conflicts between its rows.\nstatic inline void tileRelaxDisjoint(unsigned int* __restrict c, unsigned int* __restrict p,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict a,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict bSource, const size_t n,\n                                     const size_t kBase, const size_t ni, const size_t nj,\n                                     const size_t nk, unsigned int* __restrict b) {\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int* const src = bSource + kk * n;\n        unsigned int* const dst = b + kk * nj;\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n            dst[jj] = src[jj];\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (size_t ii = 0; ii < ni; ++ii) {\n        unsigned int* const cRow = c + ii * n;\n        unsigned int* const pRow = p + ii * n;\n        const unsigned int* const aRow = a + ii * n;\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n            const unsigned int aik = aRow[kk];\n            const unsigned int* const bRow = b + kk * nj;\n            const unsigned int kValue = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kk);\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n                const unsigned int candidate = aik + bRow[jj];\n                const unsigned int current = cRow[jj];\n                const bool better = candidate < current;\n                cRow[jj] = better ? candidate : current;\n                pRow[jj] = better ? kValue : pRow[jj];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Same relaxation for tiles where c overlaps a and/or b (the pivot tile and the tiles of the\n// pivot row and column). r < numTiles; ++r) {\n            const size_t k0 = r * tile;\n            const size_t nk = std::min(tile, n - k0);\n            unsigned int* const pivotDist = dist + k0 * n + k0;\n            unsigned int* const pivotPath = path + k0 * n + k0;\n\n            // Phase 1: the pivot tile depends only on itself.\n#pragma omp single\n            {\n                tileRelaxInPlace(pivotDist, pivotPath, pivotDist, pivotDist, n, k0, nk, nk, nk);\n            }\n\n            // Phase 2: the tiles of the pivot row and pivot column depend on the pivot tile.\n#pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t b = 0; ++smt) {\n        std::vector<std::vector<int>> perPackage(packages.size());\n        for (const CpuInfo& c : cpus) {\n            if (c.smt != smt) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(\n                std::lower_bound(packages.begin(), packages.end(), c.package) - packages.begin());\n            perPackage[p].push_back(c.cpu);\n        }\n        size_t remaining = 0;\n        for (std::vector<int>& v : perPackage) {\n            std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());\n            remaining += v.size();\n        }\n        if (remaining == 0) {\n            break;\n        }\n        for (size_t slot = 0; remaining > 0; ++slot) {\n            for (std::vector<int>& v : perPackage) {\n                if (slot < v.size()) {\n                    order.push_back(v[slot]);\n                    --remaining;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const size_t id = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n        cpu_set_t target;\n        CPU_ZERO(&target);\n        CPU_SET(order[id % order.size()], &target);\n        sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(target), &target);\n    }","new_string":"    // Group the hardware threads by physical core, and order the cores round-robin over the\n    // packages so that the cores in use are always spread over all sockets.\n    std::vector<std::vector<int>> cores; coreOrder.size() < cores.size(); ++slot) {\n        for (const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& list : coresPerPackage) {\n            if (slot < list.size()) {\n                coreOrder.push_back(list[slot]);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Spread the threads evenly over the cores; several threads on one core end up on its\n    // distinct SMT siblings, and consecutive thread ids stay as close together as possible so\n    // that neighbouring tiles of the static schedule share cache.\n    const size_t numThreads = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads());\n    const size_t numCores = coreOrder.size();\n    std::vector<int> assignment(numThreads);\n    for (size_t core = 0, thread = 0; core < numCores; ++core) {\n        const size_t last = (core + 1) * numThreads / numCores;\n        for (size_t sibling = 0; thread < last; ++thread, ++sibling) {\n            assignment[thread] = coreOrder[core][sibling % coreOrder[core].size()];\n        }\n    }\n\n#pragma omp parallel num_threads(numThreads)\n    {\n        const size_t id = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n        if (id < assignment.size()) {\n            cpu_set_t target;\n            CPU_ZERO(&target);\n            CPU_SET(assignment[id], &target);\n            sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(target), &target);\n        }\n    }"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":821,"cache_read_input_tokens":72006,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":821},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"217b76c4-252c-48f8-bdbc-b0e77e749810","uuid":"bf5181c5-37b3-420d-bd64-396ff9b9a70d","timestamp":"2026-09-01T19:22:25.684Z","request_id":"req_011CedGD1a6Rsp7savqreBhH"}

Offsetting the\n// path matrix by a few cache lines removes those conflicts (worth up to 7x on unlucky sizes).\nconstexpr size_t PATH_PAD_ELEMENTS = 1024;  // slack reserved at the end of the path allocation\n\nstatic unsigned int* offsetPathBase(const unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path) {\n    constexpr uintptr_t period = 4096;\n    constexpr uintptr_t target = 1088; col < numNodes; ++col) {\n            p[col] = value;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Blocked Floyd-Warshall\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Relaxation of one tile: c[i][j] = min(c[i][j], a[i][k] + b[k][j]) over the k values of the\n// tile, recording the intermediate node in p. The b tile is packed into a contiguous scratch buffer\n// first: reading it at the full matrix stride causes cache-set conflicts between its rows.\nstatic inline void tileRelaxDisjoint(unsigned int* __restrict c, unsigned int* __restrict p,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict a,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict bSource, const size_t n,\n                                     const size_t kBase, const size_t ni, const size_t nj,\n                                     const size_t nk, unsigned int* __restrict b) {\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int* const src = bSource + kk * n;\n        unsigned int* const dst = b + kk * nj;\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n            dst[jj] = src[jj];\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (size_t ii = 0; ii < ni; ++ii) {\n        unsigned int* const cRow = c + ii * n;\n        unsigned int* const pRow = p + ii * n;\n        const unsigned int* const aRow = a + ii * n;\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n            const unsigned int aik = aRow[kk];\n            const unsigned int* const bRow = b + kk * nj;\n            const unsigned int kValue = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kk);\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n                const unsigned int candidate = aik + bRow[jj];\n                const unsigned int current = cRow[jj];\n                const bool better = candidate < current;\n                cRow[jj] = better ? candidate : current;\n                pRow[jj] = better ? kValue : pRow[jj];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Same relaxation for tiles where c overlaps a and/or b (the pivot tile and the tiles of the\n// pivot row and column). Here the k loop has to stay outermost, which is what makes the in-place\n// update well defined: during step k neither c[i][k] nor c[k][j] can change, because c[k][k] is\n// zero and therefore no candidate through k improves them.\nstatic inline void tileRelaxInPlace(unsigned int* c, unsigned int* p, const unsigned int* a,\n                                    const unsigned int* b, const size_t n, const size_t kBase,\n                                    const size_t ni, const size_t nj, const size_t nk) {\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int* const bRow = b + kk * n;\n        const unsigned int kValue = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kk);\n        for (size_t ii = 0; ii < ni; ++ii) {\n            const unsigned int aik = a[ii * n + kk];\n            unsigned int* const cRow = c + ii * n;\n            unsigned int* const pRow = p + ii * n;\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n                const unsigned int candidate = aik + bRow[jj];\n                const unsigned int current = cRow[jj];\n                const bool better = candidate < current;\n                cRow[jj] = better ? candidate : current;\n                pRow[jj] = better ? kValue : pRow[jj];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Tile edge: large enough that three tiles of working set stay in the private caches while the\n// memory traffic of the whole algorithm drops by a factor of the tile size, small enough that\n// the independent tiles of the update phase keep every thread busy.\nstatic size_t chooseTileSize(const size_t numNodes, const size_t numThreads) {\n    size_t tile = 64;\n    while (tile > 16) {\n        const size_t nb = (numNodes + tile - 1) / tile;\n        if (nb > 1 && (nb - 1) * (nb - 1) >= 2 * numThreads) {\n            break;\n        }\n        tile /= 2;\n    }\n    return tile;\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(unsigned int* const dist, unsigned int* const path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    if (numNodes == 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    const size_t numThreads = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads());\n    const size_t tile = chooseTileSize(n, numThreads);\n    const size_t numTiles = (n + tile - 1) / tile;\n\n    // Blocked Floyd-Warshall. Round r applies the intermediate nodes of tile r in three\n    // dependent phases; inside each phase all tiles are independent. The result is identical to\n    // the classic triple loop, distances and predecessors alike: every (i, j) pair still sees the\n    // intermediate nodes in increasing order, and when node k is applied dist[i][k] and dist[k][j]\n    // already hold their final values, exactly as in the unblocked version.\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        std::vector<unsigned int> packBuffer(tile * tile);\n        unsigned int* const pack = packBuffer.data();\n\n        for (size_t r = 0; r < numTiles; ++r) {\n            const size_t k0 = r * tile;\n            const size_t nk = std::min(tile, n - k0);\n            unsigned int* const pivotDist = dist + k0 * n + k0;\n            unsigned int* const pivotPath = path + k0 * n + k0;\n\n            // Phase 1: the pivot tile depends only on itself.\n#pragma omp single\n            {\n                tileRelaxInPlace(pivotDist, pivotPath, pivotDist, pivotDist, n, k0, nk, nk, nk);\n            }\n\n            // Phase 2: the tiles of the pivot row and pivot column depend on the pivot tile.\n#pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t b = 0; b < numTiles; ++b) {\n                if (b == r) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                const size_t o0 = b * tile;\n                const size_t no = std::min(tile, n - o0);\n\n                unsigned int* const rowDist = dist + k0 * n + o0;\n                tileRelaxInPlace(rowDist, path + k0 * n + o0, pivotDist, rowDist, n, k0, nk, no,\n                                 nk);\n\n                unsigned int* const colDist = dist + o0 * n + k0;\n                tileRelaxInPlace(colDist, path + o0 * n + k0, colDist, pivotDist, n, k0, no, nk,\n                                 nk);\n            }\n\n            // Phase 3: every remaining tile, i.e. the bulk of the work.\n#pragma omp for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n            for (size_t bi = 0; Triangle inequality: dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] >= dist[i][j]\n    // Check a sample of paths to avoid O(n^3) validation time\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++i) This is skipped when the environment\n// already specifies a placement policy, so an explicit OMP_PROC_BIND/OMP_PLACES/GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY\n// setting always wins.\nstatic void bindThreadsToCores(const size_t numThreads) {\n    if (getenv(\"OMP_PROC_BIND\") != nullptr || getenv(\"OMP_PLACES\") != nullptr ||\n        getenv(\"GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY\") != nullptr) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    cpu_set_t allowed;\n    CPU_ZERO(&allowed);\n    if (sched_getaffinity(0, sizeof(allowed), &allowed) != 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    struct CpuInfo {\n        int cpu;\n        int package;\n        int core;\n        int smt;  // rank of this hardware thread inside its physical core\n    };\n\n    std::vector<CpuInfo> cpus;\n    for (int cpu = 0; cpu < CPU_SETSIZE; ++cpu) {\n        if (!CPU_ISSET(cpu, &allowed)) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        CpuInfo info{cpu, 0, cpu, 0};\n        char pathBuf[128];\n        snprintf(pathBuf, sizeof(pathBuf),\n                 \"/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu%d/topology/physical_package_id\", cpu);\n        if (FILE* f = fopen(pathBuf, \"r\")) {\n            if (fscanf(f, \"%d\", &info.package) != 1) {\n                info.package = 0;\n            }\n            fclose(f);\n        }\n        snprintf(pathBuf, sizeof(pathBuf), \"/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu%d/topology/core_id\", cpu);\n        if (FILE* f = fopen(pathBuf, \"r\")) {\n            if (fscanf(f, \"%d\", &info.core) != 1) {\n                info.core = cpu;\n            }\n            fclose(f);\n        }\n        cpus.push_back(info);\n    }\n    if (cpus.empty()) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Rank the hardware threads inside each physical core, in ascending cpu id order.\n    std::vector<CpuInfo> byCore = cpus;\n    std::sort(byCore.begin(), byCore.end(), [](const CpuInfo& a, const CpuInfo& b) {\n        return std::tie(a.package, a.core, a.cpu) < std::tie(b.package, b.core, b.cpu);\n    });\n    for (size_t i = 0, rank = 0; i < byCore.size(); ++i) {\n        if (i > 0 && (byCore[i].package != byCore[i - 1].package ||\n                      byCore[i].core != byCore[i - 1].core)) {\n            rank = 0;\n        } else if (i > 0) {\n            ++rank;\n        }\n        byCore[i].smt = static_cast<int>(rank);\n        for (CpuInfo& c : cpus) {\n            if (c.cpu == byCore[i].cpu) {\n                c.smt = byCore[i].smt;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Group the hardware threads by physical core, keeping the cores of a package contiguous.\n    std::vector<std::vector<int>> coreOrder;  // hardware threads of one core, smt order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < byCore.size(); ++i) {\n        if (byCore[i].smt == 0) {\n            coreOrder.emplace_back();\n        }\n        coreOrder.back().push_back(byCore[i].cpu);\n    }\n\n    // Spread the threads evenly over the cores; several threads on one core end up on its\n    // distinct SMT siblings, and consecutive thread ids stay as close together as possible so\n    // that neighbouring tiles of the static schedule share cache.\n    const size_t numCores = coreOrder.size();\n    std::vector<int> assignment(numThreads);\n    for (size_t core = 0, thread = 0; core < numCores; ++core) {\n        const size_t last = (core + 1) * numThreads / numCores;\n        for (size_t sibling = 0; thread < last; ++thread, ++sibling) {\n            assignment[thread] = coreOrder[core][sibling % coreOrder[core].size()];\n        }\n    }\n\n#pragma omp parallel num_threads(numThreads)\n    {\n        const size_t id = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n        if (id < assignment.size()) {\n            cpu_set_t target;\n            CPU_ZERO(&target);\n            CPU_SET(assignment[id], &target);\n            sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(target), &target);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Spread the pages of a matrix over the NUMA nodes of the machine via parallel first touch.\n// The vector's own value-initialization already faulted every page onto the node of the calling\n// thread, so the existing mapping is dropped first: private anonymous memory reads back as zero\n// afterwards, which is exactly the state the freshly constructed vector was in.\nstatic void firstTouchDistribute(unsigned int* const data, const size_t count) {\n    const size_t bytes = count * sizeof(unsigned int);\n    const long pageSize = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);\n    if (pageSize > 0 && bytes > static_cast<size_t>(pageSize)) {\n        const uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(data);\n        const uintptr_t pageMask = static_cast<uintptr_t>(pageSize) - 1;\n        const uintptr_t start = (base + pageMask) & ~pageMask;\n        const uintptr_t end = (base + bytes) & ~pageMask;\n        if (end > start) {\n            madvise(reinterpret_cast<void*>(start), end - start, MADV_DONTNEED);\n        }\n    }\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {\n        data[i] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\n// The kernel streams a row of `dist` and the matching row of `path` in lockstep. Both matrices\n// are large, page-aligned allocations, so their rows tend to differ by an exact multiple of the\n// L1 page-colouring period and then evict each other out of the same cache sets. Offsetting the\n// path matrix by a few cache lines removes those conflicts (worth up to 7x on unlucky sizes).\nconstexpr size_t PATH_PAD_ELEMENTS = 1024;  // slack reserved at the end of the path allocation\n\nstatic unsigned int* offsetPathBase(const unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path) {\n    constexpr uintptr_t period = 4096;\n    constexpr uintptr_t target = 1088;  // 17 cache lines apart\n    const uintptr_t delta = (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(path) -\n                             reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(dist)) % period;\n    const uintptr_t shift = (target + period - delta) % period;\n    return path + shift / sizeof(unsigned int);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Initialization\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nvoid initializeDistanceMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes,\n                              const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n\n    // Sequential: the values come from a single rand_r stream that has to be reproduced exactly.\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes * numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[i] = rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n    }\n\n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = 0; each row can therefore be filled independently.\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t row = 0; row < numNodes; ++row) {\n        unsigned int* const p = path + row * numNodes;\n        const unsigned int value = static_cast<unsigned int>(row);\n        for (size_t col = 0; col < numNodes; ++col) {\n            p[col] = value;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Blocked Floyd-Warshall\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Relaxation of one tile: c[i][j] = min(c[i][j], a[i][k] + b[k][j]) over the k values of the\n// tile, recording the intermediate node in p. Requires the destination tile to be disjoint from\n// the two source tiles, which allows the k loop to sit inside the i loop so that the destination\n// row stays hot in L1 for the whole tile. The b tile is packed into a contiguous scratch buffer\n// first: reading it at the full matrix stride causes cache-set conflicts between its rows.\nstatic inline void tileRelaxDisjoint(unsigned int* __restrict c, unsigned int* __restrict p,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict a,\n                                     const unsigned int* __restrict bSource, const size_t n,\n                                     const size_t kBase, const size_t ni, const size_t nj,\n                                     const size_t nk, unsigned int* __restrict b) {\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int* const src = bSource + kk * n;\n        unsigned int* const dst = b + kk * nj;\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n            dst[jj] = src[jj];\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (size_t ii = 0; ii < ni; ++ii) {\n        unsigned int* const cRow = c + ii * n;\n        unsigned int* const pRow = p + ii * n;\n        const unsigned int* const aRow = a + ii * n;\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n            const unsigned int aik = aRow[kk];\n            const unsigned int* const bRow = b + kk * nj;\n            const unsigned int kValue = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kk);\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n                const unsigned int candidate = aik + bRow[jj];\n                const unsigned int current = cRow[jj];\n                const bool better = candidate < current;\n                cRow[jj] = better ? candidate : current;\n                pRow[jj] = better ? kValue : pRow[jj];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Same relaxation for tiles where c overlaps a and/or b (the pivot tile and the tiles of the\n// pivot row and column). Here the k loop has to stay outermost, which is what makes the in-place\n// update well defined: during step k neither c[i][k] nor c[k][j] can change, because c[k][k] is\n// zero and therefore no candidate through k improves them.\nstatic inline void tileRelaxInPlace(unsigned int* c, unsigned int* p, const unsigned int* a,\n                                    const unsigned int* b, const size_t n, const size_t kBase,\n                                    const size_t ni, const size_t nj, const size_t nk) {\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nk; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int* const bRow = b + kk * n;\n        const unsigned int kValue = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kk);\n        for (size_t ii = 0; ii < ni; ++ii) {\n            const unsigned int aik = a[ii * n + kk];\n            unsigned int* const cRow = c + ii * n;\n            unsigned int* const pRow = p + ii * n;\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nj; ++jj) {\n                const unsigned int candidate = aik + bRow[jj];\n                const unsigned int current = cRow[jj];\n                const bool better = candidate < current;\n                cRow[jj] = better ? candidate : current;\n                pRow[jj] = better ? kValue : pRow[jj];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Below a few million matrix entries the three barriers per round and the cross-socket traffic\n// cost more than the extra cores bring in, so the thread count is scaled with the problem size.\nstatic size_t chooseThreadCount(const size_t numNodes, const size_t maxThreads) {\n    const size_t byWork = std::max<size_t>(32, numNodes * numNodes / 16384);\n    return std::max<size_t>(1, std::min(maxThreads, byWork));\n}\n\n// Tile edge: large enough that three tiles of working set stay in the private caches while the\n// memory traffic of the whole algorithm drops by a factor of the tile size, small enough that\n// the independent tiles of the update phase keep every thread busy.\nstatic size_t chooseTileSize(const size_t numNodes, const size_t numThreads) {\n    size_t tile = 48;\n    while (tile > 16) {\n        const size_t nb = (numNodes + tile - 1) / tile;\n        if (nb > 1 && (nb - 1) * (nb - 1) >= 2 * numThreads) {\n            break;\n        }\n        tile /= 2;\n    }\n    return tile;\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(unsigned int* const dist, unsigned int* const path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    if (numNodes == 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    const size_t numThreads = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads());\n    const size_t tile = chooseTileSize(n, numThreads);\n    const size_t numTiles = (n + tile - 1) / tile;\n\n    // Blocked Floyd-Warshall. Round r applies the intermediate nodes of tile r in three\n    // dependent phases; inside each phase all tiles are independent. The result is identical to\n    // the classic triple loop, distances and predecessors alike: every (i, j) pair still sees the\n    // intermediate nodes in increasing order, and when node k is applied dist[i][k] and dist[k][j]\n    // already hold their final values, exactly as in the unblocked version.\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        std::vector<unsigned int> packBuffer(tile * tile);\n        unsigned int* const pack = packBuffer.data();\n\n        for (size_t r = 0; Both files in `./floydwarshall/` were modified in place; no new files, same executable name.\n\n## What was changed\n\n**`floydwarshall.cpp`** — the kernel is now a blocked (tiled) Floyd-Warshall parallelized with OpenMP:\n\n- **Blocked algorithm** (`floydwarshall.cpp:297`): each round handles one pivot tile in three phases — pivot tile, pivot row/column panels, then all remaining tiles. Only the last phase carries the O(n³) work and its tiles are fully independent (`omp for collapse(2) schedule(static)`). This is what unlocks the speed: the naive triple loop touches n³ elements from DRAM and is ~25× memory-bound on this machine; tiling cuts that traffic by the tile size.\n- **Two tile kernels**: a `__restrict` version with the k-loop sunk innermost (destination row stays in L1) for disjoint tiles, and an in-place version with k outermost for the aliasing pivot tiles. Inner loops are branchless and `omp simd`-vectorized.\n- **B-tile packing** into a thread-local buffer — reading it at full matrix stride causes cache-set conflicts between rows (+40% at n=8192).\n- **Cache-conflict offset for `path`** (`floydwarshall.cpp:181`): `dist` and `path` rows otherwise land in identical L1 sets and evict each other. Worth up to **7×** on unlucky sizes (n=8160 went from 4.7 to 32.9 GOPS single-socket).\n- **Thread pinning** (`floydwarshall.cpp:36`): reads topology from sysfs and spreads threads over cores/sockets, respecting the process affinity mask; skipped if `OMP_PROC_BIND`/`OMP_PLACES`/`GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY` is set. Unpinned runs lose 20–60%.\n- **NUMA-aware first touch** and a parallel `path` init; the RNG fill stays sequential so the input is reproduced exactly.\n- **Thread count scaled with problem size** — at n=512 the barriers dominate, and 32 threads beat 256 by ~3×.\n\n**`CMakeLists.txt`**: `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)`, link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, add `-funroll-loops`.\n\n## Results (2× EPYC 7763, 128 cores / 256 threads)\n\n| n | original | new | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 165 ms | 15 ms | 11× |\n| 1024 | 1225 ms | 38 ms | 32× |\n| 2048 | 9459 ms | 84 ms | 113× |\n\nThread scaling at n=4096: 4.1 → 31.6 (8t) → 102.9 (32t) → 226 (128t) → 258 GOPS (256t), i.e. 55× on 128 cores over our own single-thread build, which is itself ~4× faster than the original serial code thanks to tiling.\n\n## Correctness — one caveat worth your attention\n\nThe distance matrix is **bit-identical** to the original: hashes match for n ∈ {1,2,3,7,17,48,49,64,100,127,128,129,200,255,256,257,333,512,700,1000,1024,1025} and for thread counts 1/3/7/33/default, and `-v` passes.\n\nThe internal `path` (predecessor) matrix differs in ~3% of entries. Blocking makes the pivot row/column see a round's whole k-range before the update phase consumes it, so a pair can reach its final distance at an earlier k and the later k no longer improves it — the recorded intermediate node is a different, equally valid one. I verified our `path` satisfies the witness property `dist[i][j] == dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]` with zero violations, exactly like the reference. `path` is never printed or validated by the benchmark. Reproducing the original's exact predecessor choices would require the unblocked k order and cost roughly 4–10× performance; I documented this at `floydwarshall.cpp:307` rather than giving it up. Say the word if bit-exact `path` matters and I'll switch to the unblocked variant."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":821,"cache_read_input_tokens":103677,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":821},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"217b76c4-252c-48f8-bdbc-b0e77e749810","uuid":"352fa98d-ca8c-4285-aaa3-0f8e57fccd20","timestamp":"2026-09-01T19:29:43.626Z","request_id":"req_011CedGnY8nreH5s4dSNd56b"}
